title.en: Conditions on US aircraft carrier at sea for more than 250 days raise alarms

summary.en: Thousands of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln have reportedly endured over 250 days at sea, facing severe conditions including food shortages and broken plumbing, with some expressing thoughts of self-harm.

body.en:
Thousands of US military members who have lived aboard an aircraft carrier for more than 250 days are reportedly contending with food shortages, broken plumbing and exhaustion, leading lawmakers to demand answers from the Pentagon and pressuring the Trump administration over the Iran war.

Military news outlets reported that some USS Abraham Lincoln sailors have attempted to jump overboard, and families have raised concerns about mental health onboard the ship.

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday called reports of conditions "completely misrepresented".

The carrier left California in November for the South China Sea and was sent to the Middle East ahead of attacks on Iran in February.

The deployment, which was originally set to end in May, has been repeatedly extended. No return date has been announced, but on Thursday multiple outlets reported the US is preparing to replace the carrier with the USS George Washington as part of a previously scheduled rotation plan.

Connecticut Senator Richard Blumenthal listed the reported hardships on the carrier, where about 5,000 people are on board, in a letter to Hegseth: "Shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns, and disruptions in the mail system, which have caused many care packages in route to the ship to be lost in transit for months."

"These reports warrant immediate attention," the Democrat , who serves on the Armed Services Committee, wrote, "but they also raise a broader question: whether the Navy can sustain the operational tempo now being demanded of its carrier force."

Fellow Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego called for the military to allow a congressional delegation to visit the ship and "conduct oversight investigation into this horrible situation," he posted on X, adding: "There is no reason to be denied access."

Citing two unnamed officials, CBS News, the BBC's US partner, reported that earlier this month a sailor went overboard and was recovered by a helicopter, treated by the medical department, and transferred off the ship for further care.

The Military Times and Stars and Stripes reported earlier this week that multiple service members had considered jumping overboard, according to their families. They said that being at sea for an extended period of time and the conditions on board were hurting some members' mental health.

Those conditions also reportedly included not being able to clean laundry for more than a week and not eating fresh food due to infrequent visits to ports, when troops are not always allowed to leave the ship.

T he relative of one sailor aboard the ship told BBC News that their family member has lost 65lbs (29kg) since beginning their deployment.

title.en: Engine parts smashed Ryanair window that man's head was sucked out of, report says
title.zh: 报道称，瑞安航空发动机部件砸碎窗户，男子头被吸出

summary.en: A preliminary report by US investigators says an engine fan blade broke on last month's flight from Greece to Germany.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Broken engine fragments smashed a cabin window of a Ryanair plane last month causing a man's head and right shoulder to be sucked into the hole, US investigators have said.

In a preliminary report, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said this happened after an engine fan blade broke shortly after takeoff on the 10 July flight from Greece to Germany.

Serbian national Ljubisa Karović's head and right shoulder were sucked out of the plane's window, leaving him "seriously injured and in shock".

His wife Svetlana Grković Maksimović later told BBC Serbia that she and two other passengers held on to his legs for several minutes.

In its report, the NTSB said the flight from Thessaloniki to Memmingen "experienced a No. 2 (right) engine fan-blade-out (FBO) failure during climb out".

"The crew elected to return to SKG [Thessaloniki International Airport] where they made an uneventful landing."

The NTSB was "delegated the investigation in full" by the Greek authorities in the days following the incident.

It also detailed a timeline of events given by the flight crew, who said they received a "high vibration" engine alert during the climb.

In response, they reduced the engine power and carried out a series of checks. When the vibrations stopped, the crew continued to climb on autopilot, the report said.

But the engine vibrations then increased and the crew heard a loud bang, prompting them to declare an emergency and begin their descent.

Flight attendants reported hearing and feeling the vibrations, and seeing a small amount of smoke before the oxygen masks were deployed.

One flight attendant said they then noticed passengers calling for help after a passenger became "partially lodged in a damaged cabin window", with the entire window missing.

The engine had undergone ultrasonic inspections in May this year with no findings of fault, the report stated.

Ryanair boss Michael O'Leary earlier suggested that the incident may have been caused by "foreign object damage" to an engine.
body.zh: 美国调查人员表示，上个月，瑞安航空一架飞机的发动机碎片击碎了机舱窗户，导致一名男子的头部和右肩被吸进洞里。 美国国家运输安全委员会 (NTSB) 在一份初步报告中表示，这起事故是在 7 月 10 日从希腊飞往德国的航班起飞后不久，发动机风扇叶片断裂后发生的。 塞尔维亚国民柳比萨·卡罗维奇的头部和右肩被吸出飞机的窗户，导致他“严重受伤并处于休克状态”。 他的妻子 Svetlana Grković Maksimović 后来告诉 BBC 塞尔维亚，她和另外两名乘客抓住了他的腿几分钟。 NTSB 在其报告中表示，从塞萨洛尼基飞往梅明根的航班“在爬升过程中发生了 2 号（右）发动机风扇叶片脱落 (FBO) 故障”。 “机组人员选择返回 SKG [塞萨洛尼基国际机场]，并在那里平安着陆。” 事件发生后几天，希腊当局“全面委托国家运输安全委员会进行调查”。 它还详细列出了机组人员给出的事件时间表，机组人员表示，他们在爬升过程中收到了“高振动”发动机警报。 作为回应，他们降低了发动机功率并进行了一系列检查。报告称，当振动停止后，机组人员继续在自动驾驶仪上爬升。 但随后发动机振动加剧，机组人员听到一声巨响，促使他们宣布紧急状态并开始下降。 空乘人员报告说，在氧气面罩打开之前，他们听到并感觉到了振动，并看到了少量烟雾。 一名空乘人员表示，他们随后注意到一名乘客“部分卡在受损的客舱窗户内”，整个窗户都不见了，随后乘客呼救。 报告称，该发动机于今年5月接受了超声波检查，没有发现任何故障。 瑞安航空老板迈克尔·奥利里早些时候表示，这起事件可能是由于发动机“异物损坏”造成的。

title.en: Luigi Mangione may plead guilty in federal case: report
title.zh: 路易吉·曼吉奥内可能在联邦案件中认罪：报告

summary.en: Luigi Mangione may plead guilty in a federal case charging him with stalking which would then avert a trial.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Luigi Mangione, the man accused of gunning down a health insurance executive in Manhattan, is expected to plead guilty in a federal case charging him with stalking, according to the the New York Times on Thursday.

A guilty plea would avert a trial in the closely watched case over the killing of UnitedHealth ‌Group CEO Brian Thompson, a brazen crime that was condemned by public officials but became emblematic of Americans' frustration with health insurance industry practices. It could also delay Mangione's trial next month on state murder charges.

Representatives for Mangione and the Manhattan US Attorney's Office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Mangione is due in federal court on Friday for a hearing jointly requested by his lawyers and prosecutors, who did not give a reason. A guilty plea is not guaranteed, and Mangione could change his mind before or even during the hearing. The New York Times said it was unclear what Mangione might plead guilty to and that specifics of the deal could change because talks are ongoing.

He previously pleaded not guilty in April 2025 to murder, weapons and stalking charges brought by Manhattan federal prosecutors.

US District Judge Margaret Garnett threw out the murder and weapons charges over legal technicalities in a surprise ruling in January. The decision eliminated the possibility that Mangione would face the death penalty, though he still faces a possible sentence of life without parole if convicted on the remaining stalking charges.

Mangione separately pleaded not guilty in December 2024 to state terrorism, murder, weapons and forgery charges brought by Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg. The terrorism charges were thrown out by a judge in September 2025.

A trial in that case is scheduled for September 8 before Justice Gregory Carro in Manhattan.

If he pleads guilty in the federal case, Mangione is likely to seek dismissal of the murder charge under New York's double jeopardy law, which protects people from being prosecuted twice for the same conduct. Bragg's office would oppose the move, arguing that the murder charge is legally distinct from the federal charges. Whoever loses would likely seek an emergency appeal.

Thompson led UnitedHealth Group's UNH.N insurance unit before he was shot dead 4 December 2024, outside a hotel where an investor conference was taking place.

Graphic footage of the killing and a five-day manhunt for a suspect made the case a media fixture and social media sensation. Mangione was arrested in Pennsylvania.

title.en: Romania shuts nuclear plant, Hungary dams dry Danube River
title.zh: 罗马尼亚关闭核电站，匈牙利筑坝干涸多瑙河

summary.en: Romania has shut down its only nuclear plant in a rare move prompted by the lack of cooling water from the Danube River. Hungary, meanwhile, is racing to dam the Danube, trying to keep its Paks plant online.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 由于多瑙河缺乏冷却水，罗马尼亚关闭了其唯一的核电站，这是一项罕见的举措。与此同时，匈牙利正在竞相在多瑙河上筑坝，试图保持其帕克斯核电站的正常运行。 罗马尼亚周四关闭了其唯一的核电站，这是在干旱导致多瑙河和欧洲其他主要水道水位创历史新低的情况下采取的罕见举措。 多瑙河是切尔纳沃达电厂的唯一冷却水源，该电厂通常发电量约占罗马尼亚电力的五分之一。 该电站此前仅在 2023 年因干旱和炎热的夏季而关闭过一次。 与此同时，匈牙利正忙着在多瑙河上筑坝，试图使其帕克斯核电站至少保持在最近几天维持的最低水平，远低于其容量。 罗马尼亚核电公司上个月已经关闭了切尔纳沃达的两座反应堆之一。 周四，该公司表示，“由于多瑙河水位持续大幅下降”，需要关闭第二个。 本月早些时候，该公司在海军的帮助下尝试提高工厂保持运营的机会。 最令人难忘的是，它炸毁了因低水位而暴露的岩石露头，并战略性地将岩石沉积在河床上，以将更多的水引导到切尔纳沃达。 但最终，持续的干燥天气和水位下降导致了全面关闭。 工厂厂长罗密欧·乌尔詹 (Romeo Urjan) 告诉法新社：“我们预计未来 10 天内不会重新启动。” 罗马尼亚能源部表示，正在采购替代能源，包括风电和进口能源，以确保充足的供应。尽管如此，它仍然呼吁公众负责任地消费。 它警告说，作为最后的手段，大型工业用户将不得不在晚上面临限制以节省电力。汽车制造商福特和达契亚已承诺暂停生产至 8 月 19 日，以节省电力。 周四，彼得·马扎尔总理参观了匈牙利唯一的核电站——帕克斯核电站，该电站也由多瑙河冷却。 马扎尔在布达佩斯以南约 100 公里（约 60 英里）的现场告诉记者：“我们已经开始建造低堰，这将永久有助于提高多瑙河的水位。” 九天前，该工厂面临完全关闭的风险，但政府在最后一刻中止了这些计划，因为多瑙河的水位最终比预测高了几毫米。 正常情况下，该工厂负责匈牙利约一半的...

title.en: Kennedy Center board approves Trump name on facade, renovation plan
title.zh: 肯尼迪中心董事会批准特朗普名字上墙，并制定翻修计划

summary.en: The Kennedy Center board has approved a plan to place the former US president's name on its facade, a move that appears to bypass a judge's previous ruling. This decision could lead to further legal disputes regarding the center's naming and future.
summary.zh: 肯尼迪中心董事会已批准一项计划，将前美国总统的名字刻在其外墙上，此举似乎旨在规避此前法官的一项裁决。这一决定可能引发关于该中心名称和未来的进一步法律纠纷。

body.en:
The move appears designed to circumvent a judge's ruling that the US president's name should be removed, potentially setting the stage for a new legal fight over the Kennedy Center's name and future.

The board of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts voted Thursday to add  President Donald Trump's name to the building's facade, according to US Congresswoman Joyce Beatty.

The board also voted to proceed with a two-year closure of the performing arts venue in the US capital, Washington, D.C. , for major renovations.

The decision comes after a federal judge in May ordered Trump's name to be removed from the building , ruling that only Congress can change the institution's name or authorize major alterations.

"This latest development is a transparent effort to circumvent the Court's ruling, and flies in the face of the statutes that Congress passed," Beatty, a Democrat who is also an ex-officio board member, said in a statement. "I will continue to fight for this treasured national monument."

The latest vote revives a dispute that has been unfolding since Trump reshaped the center's leadership after returning to office.

Trump became interested in the Kennedy Center's operations after winning the 2024 election. He installed a mostly handpicked board that named him chairman, and his name was added to the building's facade in December.

The move was part of a broader effort to overhaul the institution. At the time, the president also announced a two-year closure of the performing arts venue for  renovations that were scheduled to begin in July .

That decision soon faced a legal challenge. In May, Judge Christopher Cooper said, "the Kennedy Center's organic statute makes crystal clear that the Center is to be named for President Kennedy, and it cannot bear any other formal name or public memorial based on the Board's unilateral say-so."

The Kennedy Center dispute became one of several obstacles to Trump's broader efforts to remake prominent Washington landmarks. An appeals court last week halted his planned White House ballroom after he demolished the East Wing.

His Reflecting Pool renovation also faced major problems , though he still plans to build a massive Memorial Arch .

"In its meeting today, the board voted to change the front of the building's facade to read 'The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts Restored and Renovated By President Donald J. Trump,' and renamed the physical site 'the President Donald J. Trump Plaza,'" Congresswoman Beatty said.

According to The New York Times , an inscription underneath the institution's name would read: "Restored and Renovated by President Donald J. Trump."

body.zh: 此举似乎旨在规避法官关于应删除美国总统名字的裁决，这可能为围绕肯尼迪中心的名称和未来展开新的法律斗争奠定基础。 据美国国会女议员乔伊斯·比蒂称，约翰·F·肯尼迪表演艺术中心董事会周四投票决定将唐纳德·特朗普总统的名字添加到建筑物的正面。 董事会还投票决定继续关闭美国首都华盛顿特区的表演艺术场馆两​​年，进行重大整修。 这一决定是在联邦法官五月下令将特朗普的名字从大楼中删除之后作出的，裁定只有国会才能更改该机构的名称或授权进行重大改建。 “这一最新进展明显是为了规避法院的裁决，并且违背了国会通过的法规，”身为董事会当然成员的民主党人比蒂在一份声明中表示。 “我将继续为这座珍贵的国家纪念碑而奋斗。” 最新的投票重新引发了自特朗普重返办公室后重塑该中心领导层以来一直在展开的争议。 特朗普在赢得 2024 年大选后对肯尼迪中心的运营产生了兴趣。他任命了一个主要由他亲自挑选的董事会，任命他为董事长，并于 12 月将他的名字添加到了大楼的正面。 此举是对该机构进行更广泛改革的一部分。当时，总统还宣布该表演艺术场馆将关闭两年，以进行原定于 7 月开始的翻修工程。 该决定很快就面临法律挑战。五月，法官克里斯托弗·库珀表示，“肯尼迪中心的组织章程明确规定，该中心将以肯尼迪总统的名字命名，并且不能根据董事会的单方面决定而使用任何其他正式名称或公共纪念馆。” 肯尼迪中心的争端成为特朗普重塑华盛顿著名地标的更广泛努力的几个障碍之一。在他拆除东翼后，上诉法院上周叫停了他计划的白宫舞厅。 他的倒影池改造也面临重大问题，尽管他仍然计划建造一座巨大的纪念拱门。 “在今天的会议上，董事会投票决定将建筑物正面的正面改为‘唐纳德·J·特朗普总统修复和翻新的约翰·F·肯尼迪表演艺术中心’，并将实体场所重新命名为‘唐纳德·J·特朗普总统广场’，”国会女议员比蒂说。 据《纽约时报》报道，该机构名称下方的铭文写着：“由唐纳德·J·特朗普总统修复和翻新。” 该报称，这一措辞似乎是为了避免联邦法律中的一项规定……

title.en: Palestinians told to leave homes in village where Israeli settlers besieged houses
title.zh: 巴勒斯坦人在以色列定居者围困房屋的村庄被告知离开家园

summary.en: The mayor of Qusra reports that Israeli troops have been instructing families to vacate their homes, with some residences subsequently being utilized as military barracks.
summary.zh: 据库斯拉市市长报告，以色列军队一直在命令当地家庭撤离家园，其中一些房屋已被用作军营。

body.en:
About a dozen Palestinian households in a village in the occupied West Bank were told to leave their properties during an Israeli military operation to remove Israeli settlers.

The settlers had besieged residents in three homes in the area since Sunday, cutting off their power and water supplies.

Qusra Mayor, Abdel Azim Wadi, told the BBC that his village had been declared a closed military zone - and Israeli forces were using some of the vacated Palestinian houses as barracks. The Israeli military said the aim was "to protect the residents".

An Israeli spokesman told the BBC the settlers' action was "deplorable" and "unacceptable" and the government would investigate and arrest those responsible.

"The Israeli army is acting against it, and we are investigating it and we will arrest those responsible and we will prosecute them," David Mencer said.

Settlers have been emboldened by the rapid expansion of settlements under the current Israeli government – leading to a dramatic rise in settler violence as they try to drive Palestinians off their land.

Of the besieged families' three homes in Qusra, which are made up of the Abu Ridi and Hassan families, the residents of two were told to leave on Thursday, they told the BBC. They said those told to leave had since moved into the third house.

Elsewhere in the village, the residents of 11 other houses had also been told to leave by the army.

Earlier, videos shared from Qusra overnight into Thursday showed a dozen Israeli security vehicles – including a bulldozer.

In later footage – filmed in the daylight – there was a long line of Israeli security forces on the road to the Palestinian village.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said they had "dismantled two illegal outposts".

It added that it had detained one Israeli and confiscated equipment on the outskirts of the Qusra and Jalud areas, near Nablus.

One of those asked to leave their home was Qaher Odeh, who said more than 20 soldiers had entered his house on Thursday morning.

"I was asleep in the morning, my brother and I. They came in and broke down the door, shouting open up, open the door. Even now I still can't process what I saw in front of me. There was more than 20 of them, maybe 30," he said.

"We left and kept walking down towards the lower part of the neighbourhood. Shortly afterwards, they sealed off the entire area.

"There were people being forced out of their homes. A lot of people," Odeh added.

After around 10 hours some families were allowed to return to their homes but found them upturned. One man told us the soldiers had thrown all the food out the fridge and stolen $1,500 in cash (£1,112).

"The soldiers were instructed that the Qusra residents will remain in their homes," the IDF said.

body.zh: 在以色列驱逐以色列定居者的军事行动期间，被占领的约旦河西岸一个村庄的大约十几户巴勒斯坦家庭被告知离开他们的财产。 自周日以来，定居者围困了该地区三处房屋的居民，切断了他们的电力和供水。 库斯拉市长阿卜杜勒·阿齐姆·瓦迪告诉英国广播公司，他的村庄已被宣布为军事禁区，以色列军队正在使用一些空出的巴勒斯坦房屋作为军营。以色列军方表示，此举的目的是“保护居民”。 以色列发言人告诉英国广播公司，定居者的行为“令人遗憾”且“不可接受”，政府将调查并逮捕责任人。 大卫·门瑟说：“以色列军队正在对此采取行动，我们正在对此进行调查，我们将逮捕责任人并起诉他们。” 现任以色列政府领导下的定居点迅速扩张，让定居者更加胆大妄为，导致定居者的暴力行为急剧增加，因为他们试图将巴勒斯坦人赶出自己的土地。 他们告诉英国广播公司，在库斯拉被围困的三户人家中，有阿布里迪和哈桑一家，其中两户的居民周四被告知离开。他们说，那些被告知离开的人已经搬进了第三栋房子。 在村里的其他地方，另外11户人家的居民也被军队告知离开。 早些时候，Qusra 从夜间到周四分享的视频显示，有十几辆以色列安全车辆，其中包括一辆推土机。 在后来在白天拍摄的镜头中，以色列安全部队在通往巴勒斯坦村庄的路上排起了长队。 以色列国防军（IDF）表示，他们已经“拆除了两个非法哨所”。 它还补充说，它在纳布卢斯附近的库斯拉和贾鲁德地区郊区拘留了一名以色列人并没收了设备。 Qaher Odeh 是其中一名被要求离开家的人，他说周四早上有 20 多名士兵进入他的家。 “早上我和我的兄弟正在睡觉。他们进来并破门而入，大喊开门，开门。即使现在我仍然无法处理我面前所看到的事情。他们有 20 多个，也许有 30 个，”他说。 “我们离开后继续朝街区的低处走去。不久之后，他们封锁了整个地区。 “有人被迫离开家园。很多人，”奥德补充道。 大约10个小时后，一些家庭被允许返回家中，但发现家中的房屋被翻倒了。一名男子告诉我们，士兵们把冰箱里的所有食物都扔了出来，并偷走了 1,500 美元现金（1,112 英镑）。 以色列国防军表示：“士兵们接到指示，库斯拉居民将留在家中。” 它补充说，士兵不会...

reflection.en: This verse reminds us of the profound vulnerability of people when powerful forces act without restraint. It calls us to recognize the suffering of those displaced from their homes and to pray for justice and protection for the helpless.

title.en: Romania shuts only nuclear plant as heat causes huge drop in Danube River level
title.zh: 酷热致多瑙河水位骤降，罗马尼亚关闭唯一核电站

summary.en: Romania's sole nuclear power plant, Cernavodă, has been shut down due to a significant drop in the Danube River's water level caused by extreme heat. The plant, which supplies 20% of the country's electricity, is expected to remain offline for at least ten days.
summary.zh: 罗马尼亚唯一的核电站切尔纳沃德核电站因酷热导致多瑙河水位大幅下降而关闭。该电站供应罗马尼亚20%的电力，预计将停运至少十天。

body.en:
Romania has shut down its only nuclear power station because of extremely low water levels in the Danube river caused by prolonged hot weather affecting much of Europe.

The Cernavodă plant, where two reactors produce about 20% of Romania's electricity, is not expected to be restarted within the next 10 days.

Earlier this week, authorities tried to increase the water flow to the plant - which uses the Danube for cooling - by sinking barges loaded with rocks in the river.

Neighbouring Hungary has so far avoided a shutdown of its only nuclear plant in Paks, which also uses the Danube. The waters in Europe's second-longest river have fallen to the lowest levels for 30 years in several countries.

The second of the two 706-megawatt reactors at Cernavodă was disconnected from the Romanian electricity grid just before midday on Thursday.

"We do not foresee a restart within the next 10 days," plant director Romeo Urjan told the AFP news agency.

The shortfall in power is usually covered by solar and wind during the hot, windy daytimes - but traditional coal- and gas-powered generation will have to be supplemented by imports during the evenings.

Romania also has huge hydropower capacity, although that has been heavily cut by the same low river levels that caused the nuclear shutdown.

In Hungary, Prime Minister Péter Magyar warned last month that the Soviet-era Paks, which has four nuclear reactors, could be forced to shut down entirely for the first time.

Plant officials said that levels in the Danube were so low that the suction nozzles used to take in water could not reach it.

Climate change is driving up temperatures around the world - but particularly in Europe.

It is the fasting warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus climate service.

This is causing increased summer heatwaves, greater pressure on Europe's waters and more intense wildfires.

The Rhine - another of Europe's key waterway - is also suffering low water levels, which is severely limiting traffic.

Italy's largest agricultural trade association, Coldiretti, said climate-related damage - such as hail, drought and wildfires could exceed €3bn (£2.6bn; $3.5bn).

France's Environment Minister Monique Barbut warned that data from the country's national statistics agency suggested the recent heatwaves could rack up €10bn to €15bn in direct and indirect costs.

The Dutch bank Triodos said the extreme heat and its consequences could wipe out much of the projected economic growth for the EU.

The European Commission had forecast growth of 1.1%, while the IMF expected the euro area to grow by around 0.9%.

body.zh: 由于欧洲大部分地区持续炎热天气导致多瑙河水位极低，罗马尼亚关闭了其唯一的核电站。 切尔纳沃德核电站的两座反应堆提供罗马尼亚约 20% 的电力，预计未来 10 天内不会重新启动。 本周早些时候，当局试图通过在河中沉没满载岩石的驳船来增加流向该工厂的水流量，该工厂利用多瑙河进行冷却。 邻国匈牙利迄今为止避免了其位于帕克斯的唯一核电站的关闭，该核电站也使用多瑙河。欧洲第二长河流的水位在多个国家已降至30年来的最低水平。 切尔纳沃德两座 706 兆瓦反应堆中的第二座于周四中午之前与罗马尼亚电网断开。 工厂主管罗密欧·乌尔詹 (Romeo Urjan) 告诉法新社：“我们预计未来 10 天内不会重新启动。” 在炎热多风的白天，电力缺口通常由太阳能和风能来弥补，但传统的煤炭和天然气发电在晚上则必须通过进口来补充。 罗马尼亚也拥有巨大的水力发电能力，尽管由于河流水位较低而导致核电站停运，水力发电能力大幅削减。 在匈牙利，总理彼得·马扎尔上个月警告说，拥有四个核反应堆的苏联时代帕克斯可能首次被迫完全关闭。 工厂官员表示，多瑙河的水位很低，用于吸水的吸嘴无法到达。 气候变化正在推高世界各地的气温，尤其是在欧洲。 根据哥白尼气候服务机构的数据，这是一个快速变暖的大陆，升温速度是全球平均水平的两倍。 这导致夏季热浪加剧、欧洲水域压力加大以及野火更加猛烈。 欧洲另一条主要水道莱茵河也面临低水位，严重限制了交通。 意大利最大的农业贸易协会 Coldiretti 表示，冰雹、干旱和野火等与气候相关的损失可能超过 30 亿欧元（26 亿英镑；35 亿美元）。 法国环境部长 Monique Barbut 警告称，该国国家统计局的数据显示，最近的热浪可能造成 100 亿至 150 亿欧元的直接和间接成本。 荷兰特里奥多斯银行表示，极端高温及其后果可能会抵消欧盟预计的大部分经济增长。 欧盟委员会预计增长1.1%，而国际货币基金组织预计欧元区增长0.9%左右。 周五，希腊热门度假胜地希维里 (Siviri) 和福尔卡 (Fourka) 的 200 多人（其中大部分是游客）被疏散。

reflection.en: The shutdown of Romania's nuclear plant due to low river levels reminds us of our deep dependence on the natural world. Yahweh placed humanity in creation to "work it and take care of it," a call to responsible stewardship. This event underscores the interconnectedness of our energy systems with the health of our environment.
reflection.zh: 罗马尼亚核电站因河流水位过低而关闭，这提醒我们人类对自然界的深切依赖。雅伟将人类安置在受造界中，是要我们“耕种看守”，这是对负责任的管家职分的呼召。这一事件强调了我们的能源系统与环境健康之间的相互关联。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
verse.textZh: 雅伟神将那人安置在伊甸园，使他修理看守。

title.en: Family of Irish plane crash victim awarded $29m in damages
title.zh: 爱尔兰空难受害者家属获赔 2900 万美元

summary.en: A jury in Chicago in the US awarded the sum to Michael Ryan's family after his widow Naoise Connolly Ryan brought a civil suit against Boeing.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The widow of an Irish United Nations employee, who died in 2019 following a Boeing 737 Max crash in Ethiopia, has been awarded $29m (£21.5m) in damages.

A jury in Chicago in the United States awarded the sum to Michael 'Mick' Ryan's family after his widow Naoise Connolly Ryan brought a civil suit against the aircraft manufacturer.

Her lawyers have said the verdict "represents an important measure of accountability and justice".

A Boeing spokesperson said the company is "deeply sorry to all who lost loved ones" and they "respect" the right for families to "pursue their claims".

Michael Ryan, a father of two living in Cork but originally from County Clare, was among the 157 people killed on board the Ethiopian Airlines plane.

Lawyer Steven C Marks, who represented Ryan's widow, said: "While no financial award can ever replace a life or undo the profound loss his family has endured, we are grateful that the jury carefully considered the evidence and reached this decision."

Marks said that Connolly Ryan has "pursued justice for Mick with extraordinary strength and determination" and his firm Podhurst Orseck have been "honoured to stand beside her in her unwavering pursuit to hold Boeing accountable".

"Although the verdict marks a significant milestone, the broader effort to hold Boeing responsible for this tragedy, and to help prevent anything like it from happening again, is just as important," he added.

In a statement, a Boeing spokesperson said: "We are deeply sorry to all who lost loved ones on Lion Air Flight 610 and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302.

"While we have resolved nearly all of these claims through settlements, families are entitled to pursue their claims through the court process, and we respect their right to do so."

On a United Nations memorial page to Michael Ryan , external it said he helped the World Food Programme "bring assistance to vulnerable people" in Afghanistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Ethiopia and Bangladesh.

The organisation credits him with organising "the building of shelters and infrastructure" in Bangladesh "which saved tens of thousands of Rohingya refugees from the threat of landslides and floods".

It also said he built medical centres in Liberia during the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak.

Marks told BBC News NI that Ryan "will be missed by the world at large" as that was "who he served".

"It's tragic to the public, but it pales in comparison to the loss for the family.

Flight ET302 took off from Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa at 08:38 local time (05:38 GMT) on 10 March for a two-hour flight to the Kenyan capital, Nairobi.

Six minutes later, at 08:44, it crashed 30 miles southeast of the airport , near the town of Bishoftu.

The impact was so great, both engines were buried at a depth of 10m (32ft), in a crater 28m wide...
body.zh: 一名爱尔兰联合国雇员于 2019 年在埃塞俄比亚波音 737 Max 坠机事故中丧生，她的遗孀获得了 2900 万美元（2150 万英镑）的赔偿。 在迈克尔·“米克”·瑞安的遗孀 Naoise Connolly Ryan 对飞机制造商提起民事诉讼后，美国芝加哥的一个陪审团将这笔赔偿金判给了迈克尔·“米克”·瑞安的家人。 她的律师表示，这一判决“代表了问责和正义的重要举措”。 波音发言人表示，该公司“对所有失去亲人的人深感抱歉”，并“尊重”家属“寻求索赔”的权利。 迈克尔·瑞安 (Michael Ryan) 是两个孩子的父亲，居住在科克，但来自克莱尔郡，他是埃塞俄比亚航空公司飞机上遇难的 157 人之一。 瑞安遗孀的代表律师史蒂文·C·马克斯表示：“虽然任何经济赔偿都无法取代生命，也无法挽回他家人所遭受的巨大损失，但我们很感激陪审团仔细考虑了证据并做出了这一决定。” 马克斯表示，康诺利·瑞安“以非凡的力量和决心为米克伸张正义”，而他的公司 Podhurst Orseck 也“很荣幸能站在她身边，坚定不移地追究波音的责任”。 他补充说：“尽管这一判决标志着一个重要的里程碑，但让波音公司对这场悲剧负责并帮助防止类似事件再次发生的更广泛努力也同样重要。” 波音发言人在一份声明中表示：“我们对所有在狮航 610 航班和埃塞俄比亚航空 302 航班上失去亲人的人深感抱歉。 “虽然我们已经通过和解解决了几乎所有这些索赔，但家庭有权通过法庭程序提出索赔，我们尊重他们这样做的权利。” 联合国在迈克尔·瑞安的纪念页面上对外表示，他帮助世界粮食计划署在阿富汗、斯里兰卡、尼泊尔、埃塞俄比亚和孟加拉国“为弱势群体提供援助”。 该组织称赞他在孟加拉国组织了“庇护所和基础设施建设”，“使数以万计的罗兴亚难民免受山体滑坡和洪水的威胁”。 它还说，他在2014-16年埃博拉疫情爆发期间在利比里亚建立了医疗中心。 马克斯告诉英国广播公司新闻网，瑞安“将被全世界怀念”，因为“他所服务的人”。 “这对公众来说是一场悲剧，但与家庭的损失相比就显得苍白无力了。 3月10日当地时间08:38（格林威治标准时间05:38）ET302航班从埃塞俄比亚首都亚的斯亚贝巴起飞，飞行两个小时飞往肯尼亚首都内罗毕。 六分钟后，即 08:44，飞机在机场东南 30 英里处坠毁，地点靠近 Bishoftu 镇。 撞击如此之大，两台发动机都被埋在 10m（32 英尺）深、宽 28m 的陨石坑中……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: US disputes reports of trying conditions on carrier in Gulf
title.zh: 美国对海湾地区航母试验条件的报道提出异议

summary.en: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called reports of poor conditions and mental health strain aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier in the Middle East "completely misrepresented." Senators want an investigation.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯称，有关中东亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰条件恶劣和精神健康紧张的报道“完全失实”。参议员们希望进行调查。 美国国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯为亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰的状况进行了辩护，该航母在八个多月的时间里在海上度过了创纪录的天数，仅在港口短暂停留。 赫格斯称美国两家军事媒体《海军时报》和《星条旗报》最近的报道“完全失实”。 报道援引水手亲属的话说，船上条件恶劣，甚至有一名船员试图跳海，但遭到挫败。 这艘载有 5,000 人的航空母舰于 11 月离开圣地亚哥，前往太平洋部署。 随后它被改道飞往中东，为特朗普白宫所谓的“史诗愤怒行动”做好准备，并自一月份以来在与伊朗的战争中一直在波斯湾或更广泛的地区。 赫格斯周四在访问巴拿马时对记者表示：“我们确保每艘船、每名船员、每名船长每时每刻都拥有我们所能提供的一切。” “有些部署时间比其他部署时间长，我对这些水手比任何人都更加尊重和感激。他们在公海、在恶劣条件下、港口停靠次数较少的情况下所做的事情令人难以置信。” 更长时间的海上部署，特别是在压力和危险程度更高、休息和娱乐机会更少的战时，一直是美国海军面临的挑战。 一天前，亚利桑那州参议员鲁本·加莱戈表示，他呼吁两党参议院代表团对亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰进行正式监督访问，以“调查令人震惊的情况”。 “与唐纳德·特朗普不同，我见过现役军人，”加列戈说。 “他在进行这场非法战争时对待我们军人的方式不仅令人厌恶，而且很危险。这些水手应该知道他们什么时候会回家。” 加莱戈周四重申了这一呼吁，称国会“需要履行其职责并让本届政府承担责任”。 参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔还呼吁海军考虑航空母舰上的情况，并指出“广泛报道称林肯号上存在基本物资短缺、水污染、管道问题、心理健康恶化、甲板安全问题”以及其他问题。 《海军时报》和《星条旗报》几个月来一直关注亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰创纪录的部署，但本周两者都重新深入探讨了这一问题。上周晚些时候，家人直接提出上诉……

title.en: When the earth moves: six major earthquakes of 2026
title.zh: 当地球移动时：2026年六次大地震

summary.en: Colombia, Venezuela, Mindanao: Thousands have died in powerful earthquakes this year. Six such events show that the magnitude of the quake is not the only factor determining the scale of the disaster.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Colombia, Venezuela, Mindanao: Thousands have died in powerful earthquakes this year. Six such events show that the magnitude of the quake is not the only factor determining the scale of the disaster.

Is 2026 a particularly bad year for earthquakes ? The number of extremely strong quakes so far this year is not, in fact, unusual. Over the long term, around the world, there are an average of about 15 earthquakes per year registering above magnitude 7 on the Richter scale. By mid-August this year, there had been 10. The devastation some of the quakes have wreaked has, however, been striking.

On June 24, Venezuela was hit by an earthquake that proved to be by far the deadliest this year. A magnitude 7.2 quake was followed just 39 seconds later by an even stronger one of magnitude 7.5. The north of the country and the capital, Caracas, were the areas worst affected.

According to official figures, more than 6,300 people were killed in the double earthquake. The effects on the impoverished country's infrastructure have also been dramatic. Shortly afterward, a satellite-based assessment by researchers at Oregon State University provisionally concluded that more than 58,000 buildings may have been damaged or destroyed.

With a magnitude of 7.8, the earthquake on June 8 off the southern coast of the Philippine island of Mindanao was the strongest of 2026 so far. It occurred at a depth of about 57 kilometers (35 miles), and was felt across large parts of the island.

At least 107 people were killed. But the fact that, despite the very high magnitude of the quake, far fewer people died in the Philippines than in Venezuela demonstrates that the strength of the quake does not necessarily determine the severity of the consequences.

On August 10, a magnitude 7.4 earthquake shook western Colombia . The epicenter was in the Choco region, near San Jose del Palmar. Although the quake occurred at a depth of 100 kilometers (62 miles), the damage it caused was immense.

More than 250 people are currently estimated to have died. Landslides and damaged roads are hampering the search for victims buried beneath the rubble, as well as the provision of supplies to remote areas. After Venezuela, this quake is the most consequential so far this year for Latin America.

On March 24, the earth shook near the island group of Vava'u in the Pacific kingdom of Tonga . With a magnitude of 7.5, it was one of the strongest globally this year. But because there was no severe damage and no deaths, it received almost no attention from the media.

The quake occurred unusually far below the earth's crust, at a depth of around 230 kilometers (143 miles), meaning that the tremors were significantly weakened by the time they reached the surface. To date, there have been no reports of deaths,...

title.en: Trump's fiercest defender? Five moments defining Karoline Leavitt's time as press secretary

body.en:
Karoline Leavitt is leaving her post as White House press secretary after 20 months marked by fierce loyalty to United States President Donald Trump and fiery clashes with the media.

As Trump's highest-ranking spokesperson, the 28-year-old became known for her unwavering defences of the president, her embrace of MAGA and "new media" voices including podcasters and influencers, and her amplification of false, misleading and highly contentious claims from the podium.

Trump announced she was leaving her role at the end of the month to spend more time with her family, and would continue to serve as one of his "top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party". Leavitt has two young children, the first born during Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and the second in May this year.

She was the first White House press secretary history to give birth while serving in the role, and the youngest person ever to hold the position.

Leavitt has been press secretary since Trump returned to office in January last year, making her the president's second-longest-serving press secretary after Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who served from 2017 to 2019.

Trump's next press secretary will be his sixth across two terms. He is yet to indicate who may replace Leavitt.

Leavitt and White House communications director Steven Cheung revamped the Trump administration's already-confrontational posture toward the media.

The Trump administration began handpicking which journalists would receive access to the president, overhauling the long-running system established by the independent White House Correspondents Association.

The "press pool" was traditionally a rotation chosen by the industry group to ensure media outlets had uniform access to the president and could relay his activities to the public and to other journalists who could not attend smaller gatherings.

In one of Leavitt's first moves as press secretary last year, she introduced a "new media seat" in the White House briefing room. Continuing Trump's longstanding attacks on establishment journalists, she vowed to give new media voices a more prominent role in covering his presidency.

"We welcome independent journalists, podcasters, social media influencers and content creators to apply for credentials to cover this White House," she said in January 2025.

While some commentators characterised it as recognition of a changing media landscape, others accused the administration of using it as a lever to reward outlets whose coverage was viewed as favourable towards the president.

title.en: 'Automatically ineligible': New Eurovision rule changes who can host the contest
title.zh: “自动失去资格”：欧洲歌唱大赛新规则改变了谁可以主办比赛

summary.en: Organizers of the Eurovision contest have announced new rule changes, stating that these adjustments are intended to offer enhanced clarity and safeguard the integrity of the competition.
summary.zh: 欧洲歌唱大赛的组织者宣布了新的规则修改，称这些调整旨在提供更大的清晰度并保护比赛的完整性。

body.en:
Eurovision Song Contest organisers announced overnight they were excluding any country involved in an armed conflict from hosting the competition and increased the minimum age of competitors.

While they did not mention any country by name, Israel, which has been at war in Gaza since 2023 , came close to winning the competition in both 2025 and 2026, ultimately finishing second on each occasion.

Under the old rules, the winning country normally hosts the following year's competition.

Under the new rules, "the winning broadcaster will automatically be ineligible to host the contest if an armed conflict, a sensitive geopolitical situation, or any other situation materially affects the security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region", the organisers said in a statement.

In a first, five countries — Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Iceland — boycotted the 2026 competition in Vienna over Israel's participation.

They said they could not take part alongside Israel because of its war in Gaza .

A United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the UN as a whole and has been criticised by Israel, concluded in September 2025 that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

Israel is separately defending a genocide case at the International Court of Justice (ICJ), which has ordered Israel to implement provisional measures to ensure genocidal actions are not committed in Gaza, but has yet to issue a final ruling.

Martin Green, director of the Eurovision Song Contest, said in a statement that the changes had been guided by feedback from member countries.

He added: "These changes are about giving everyone involved greater clarity, protecting artists and ensuring the contest continues to provide a safe and welcoming environment, while preserving the spirit and integrity that make the Eurovision Song Contest so special."

The organisers also announced that competitors must be at least 18, up from 16, on the day of their first rehearsal.

"This change continues the work already undertaken by the contest to strengthen safeguarding and protect younger artists from the pressures associated with competing at the Eurovision Song Contest," they added in the statement.

The youngest person to win the contest was 13-year-old Sandra Kim from Belgium in 1986, according to Eurovision records.

Eurovision is a co-production of public broadcasters belonging to the European Broadcasting Union. Since the EBU includes members from outside Europe, the contest is not limited to European countries.

title.en: Israeli settlers keep up siege of Palestinian homes in West Bank after clashes with troops
title.zh: 与军队发生冲突后，以色列定居者继续围攻约旦河西岸的巴勒斯坦房屋

summary.en: Residents said they were left without food and medicine, while the military condemned the settlers’ actions.

body.en:
The Israeli military said overnight it would deploy additional troops to restore order after failing to end a blockade by Israeli settlers of Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank.

The siege began on Sunday, when settlers erected a makeshift tent near homes in the Palestinian village of Qusra, south of Nablus, preventing essential food and medical supplies from reaching residents.

Israeli troops clashed with the settlers while trying to disperse them from the outpost they set up directly in front of Palestinian homes, according to witnesses.

The incident marked a rare confrontation between settlers and the military and comes amid a sharp increase in settler land seizures and attacks on Palestinians.

All Israeli settlements and outposts in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"We have received no food and no medicine," Qusai Abu Rida, a Palestinian trapped inside one of the houses, told the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency by telephone, adding that he had only managed to secure electricity thanks to solar panels.

The Israeli military condemned the settlers' actions and declared the area a "closed military zone", removing their tent on Wednesday morning (local time).

By mid-afternoon, an AFP photographer at the scene said the military had left and the tent had been removed, but the settlers were still there.

"The army has withdrawn, and so far we are still besieged, with the settlers at our doorstep," he said.

Later on Wednesday, the military announced it would send an additional infantry battalion and that more soldiers would be on standby.

The chief of the general staff "directed that efforts to strengthen order and operational control in the area continue, as well as efforts to prevent further serious incidents", a military statement said.

A day earlier, the Israeli military said it had received reports of settlers entering and taking control of Palestinian homes and land in the area.

"This is illegal, reprehensible and unacceptable activity that harms the residents of the areas and disrupts their daily lives," it said.

It also said that disciplinary action would be taken against security personnel who had been filmed at the site days earlier.

Violence by Israeli settlers towards Palestinians in the West Bank has persisted for years , often with little or no legal consequence, but recent months have seen a surge in attacks .

Last Sunday, Israel's military closed the West Bank village of Taybeh to non-residents to prevent growing attacks on Palestinians by Israeli settlers. Taybeh is one of the only Christian villages remaining in the West Bank.

title.en: Zhu Rongji, who helped turn China into a trading giant, dies at 97
title.zh: 曾帮助中国成为贸易大国的朱镕基去世，享年97岁

summary.en: The former premier brought China into the WTO and championed reforms that fuelled growth.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, who spearheaded China's entry into global trade and laid the foundation for its explosive growth, has died at the age of 97.

He served in the country's second-highest office from 1998-2003 and played a leading role in securing its entry into the World Trade Organization, opening Chinese factories to the international market and drawing foreign investment.

He was one of the most important economic reformers who moved local tax powers to the central government, closed or privatised failing state firms and promoted home ownership.

Many in China remember him as a tough and pragmatic leader who delivered double-digit growth and was rarely afraid to speak his mind.

In 1998, he said China was facing "many potential crises that could erupt at any time...

"Ordinary people are discontent about us in many ways. Especially, there is corruption among officials, the gulf between rich and poor and the way some local officials act like tyrants."

He labelled rogue bankers as "half-wits" and said the dams and flood dykes lining the Yangtze River were as "flimsy and porous as tofu dregs".

Under his leadership, which helped stabilise the economy and tackle corruption, China began transforming into a manufacturing powerhouse, leaving behind its status as a Communist outsider.

Though he faced criticism because those reforms also led to 30 million lay-offs over five years, and with huge growth came more inequality.

Chinese state media describe Zhu Rongji's life as one of "revolution, struggle and brilliance".

He was born in the central province of Hunan in 1928 and earned a degree in electrical engineering before joining the civil service.

He joined the Communist Party in 1949, but was purged twice - first after criticising Mao Zedong's economic policies as "irrational" and being labelled a "rightist", and again during the Cultural Revolution.

Zhu was brought back into the fold after Mao's death, and by 1991 had risen to the role of vice-premier in charge of China's economy.

Zhu led China through difficult negotiations to enter the World Trade Organization in 2002.

In state media his obituary described him as an "outstanding member of the Communist Party of China and loyal Commnist fighter... an outstanding leader of the Party and state".
body.zh: 中国前总理朱镕基去世，享年97岁。朱镕基是中国进入全球贸易的带头人，为中国的爆炸性增长奠定了基础。 1998年至2003年，他在中国第二高职位任职，在确保中国加入世界贸易组织、中国工厂向国际市场开放和吸引外国投资方面发挥了主导作用。 他是最重要的经济改革家之一，他将地方税收权力移交给中央政府，关闭或私有化破产的国有企业，并促进住房所有权。 许多中国人都记得他是一位强硬而务实的领导人，实现了两位数的增长，并且从不害怕说出自己的想法。 1998年，他表示中国面临“许多随时可能爆发的潜在危机…… “普通人在很多方面对我们不满。特别是官员腐败、贫富差距和一些地方官员的暴君行为。” 他将流氓银行家称为“笨蛋”，并称长江沿岸的水坝和防洪堤“像豆腐渣一样脆弱、多孔”。 在他的领导下，中国稳定了经济并解决了腐败问题，开始转变为制造业强国，摆脱了共产主义局外人的地位。 但他也面临批评，因为这些改革也导致五年内 3000 万人失业，而且巨大的增长带来了更多的不平等。 中国官方媒体将朱镕基的一生描述为“革命、奋斗、辉煌”的一生。 他 1928 年出生于中部湖南省，在加入公务员队伍之前获得了电气工程学位。 他于1949年加入共产党，但两次遭到清洗——第一次是在批评毛泽东的经济政策“非理性”并被贴上“右派”标签之后，第二次是在文化大革命期间。 毛泽东去世后，朱重回国门，并于 1991 年升任副总理，主管中国经济。 2002年，朱镕基带领中国通过艰难的谈判加入世界贸易组织。 官方媒体的讣告将他描述为“优秀的中国共产党党员、忠诚的共产主义战士……党和国家的杰出领导人”。

title.en: The China factor in the United States' $500 million move in a tiny Australian town
title.zh: 美国在澳大利亚小镇投资5亿美元的“中国因素”

summary.en: The Pentagon is investing $500 million in a small Australian town in New South Wales, a move attributed to strategic considerations related to China. The reason for this sudden interest in a town of only 130 people is its role in broader international geopolitical dynamics.
summary.zh: 五角大楼正在澳大利亚新南威尔士州的一个小镇投资5亿美元，此举被认为是与中国相关的战略考量。这个只有130人的小镇突然受到关注，是因为它在全球地缘政治动态中的作用。

body.en:
The town of Fifield near Parkes is about a six-hour drive west of Sydney, and at the last Census was home to about 130 people. Now, the town has found itself at the centre of a major strategic play by the United States government.

The US Department of War has committed to make a conditional loan of US$400 million (about $566 million) to Sunrise Energy Metals, an Australian mining company hoping to deliver the world’s first supply of a key critical mineral outside of China.

Scandium is listed as a critical mineral in both Australia and the US, signalling its strategic importance in aerospace and defence.

This loan is another chapter in the US government’s search for secure critical mineral supply chains to reduce its dependency on Chinese supply. But success will require sustained investment and government support.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Scandium is a highly strategic metal used to produce ultra-high-strength alloys needed for the most advanced fighter jets. It is also used in solid oxide fuel cells, crucial for providing reliable power to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

First, demand for scandium is being driven by massive increases in defence spending across North America, Europe and Asia and an investment boom in power-hungry AI data centres.

Second, China’s sweeping export controls on rare earth elements, including scandium, have contributed to a persistent shortage of supply on the global market, pushing up prices.

These export controls are designed to maintain China’s dominance of supply chains for key critical minerals and slow down the US defence and industrial base.

Still, the market for scandium is tiny. According to statistics from the US Geological Survey, the entire world only consumed 60 tonnes of the metal in 2025.

Scandium is usually found in very small quantities. For that reason, until now, it has been exclusively produced as a byproduct of nickel and titanium processing.

This is what sets the Sunrise Energy Metals project apart — the proposed mine has scandium deposits in a high enough concentration to be the first primary source of scandium in the world.

If production goes ahead, and lives up to its promise of producing 60 tonnes of high-purity scandium each year by 2028, this would be enough to completely satisfy the current level of global demand.

According to the company, there is also potential to expand the project in the future and add another 120 tonnes of production.

The deal gives the US government first rights to purchase scandium from Sunrise Energy Metals, with production expected to start in late 2028.

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华大使指出，“世界观差异”是澳中两国建立健康关系的主要障碍之一。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

body.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华最高外交官表示，由于世界观不匹配，澳大利亚不太可能与中国建立真正的伙伴关系，因此追求这一目标毫无意义。 但澳大利亚前驻华大使格雷厄姆·弗莱彻在洛伊研究所的一篇分析文章中指出，一些不确定因素，例如中国在台湾的军事行动，仍然可能破坏两国关系的“适度新常态”。 他说，2022 年联邦选举中的政府更迭为两国之间日益令人担忧的交易起到了断路器的作用，尽管它们仍然受到涉及中国军队的恐吓性军事冲突的损害。 在澳大利亚和斐济签署具有里程碑意义的共同防御联盟后，中国于 7 月向南太平洋发射弹道导弹，引发了国际社会的广泛谴责。 在时任总理斯科特·莫里森 (Scott Morrison) 的领导下，新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情期间外交紧张局势达到顶峰后，阿尔巴尼亚政府寻求稳定与中国的关系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 中国对澳大利亚出口产品实施了价值 200 亿美元的贸易制裁，但这些措施已慢慢取消。 中国是澳大利亚最大的贸易伙伴，也是该国约三分之一出口的目的地。 弗莱彻表示，中国并未放弃将澳大利亚拉近其轨道的希望，而澳大利亚则更专注于巩固当前的关系。 “但这种关系不太可能变得真正亲密——就像澳大利亚与其地区及其他地方志同道合的伙伴所享有的轻松、亲密的友谊一样，”他说。 “世界观和国家安全议程的分歧实在太大了。 “堪培拉追求这样的目标是毫无意义的；它认识到这一点并且是现实的。” 世界观的“不匹配”使得两国关系容易受到破坏，其主要风险包括新一轮严重分歧或爆发冲突，包括对台湾使用武力。 这位前外交官表示：“动乱或冲突总是有可能发生，尽管我认为目前可能性不大。” 弗莱彻表示，如果政策得到跨党派支持，并且政客们不“寻求利用困难谋取国内利益”，那么澳大利亚在面对中国时将会更加坚定。 “两党合作带来了政策的一致性，并限制了中国在澳大利亚体系内玩弄游戏的能力，”他说。 弗莱彻于 2019 年至 2023 年担任澳大利亚驻中国大使，并于 2014 年领导谈判团队，帮助两国签署了自由贸易协定……

Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peace actively, recognizing that while complete agreement may not always be possible, our commitment to peaceful coexistence remains vital. title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，逾百万人撤离，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," he said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

Fujian maritime authorities said 55 coastal passenger ferry routes had been suspended, all 115 offshore construction projects had been halted, and 290 construction vessels had been moved to sheltered waters.

title.en: A third Sydney airport runway incident under investigation
title.zh: 悉尼机场第三起跑道事件正在调查中

summary.en: A safety investigation is underway into a third near-collision incident in as many weeks at Sydney airport.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia's transport safety watchdog has launched an investigation into a third near-collision incident between two planes at Sydney airport in as many weeks.

The potential collision happened just hours after a similar incident last week made national and international headlines and sparked widespread safety concerns. A crew member was injured in that incident.

The Australian Transport Safety Bureau announced on Thursday night that it had commenced an investigation into the runway incursion involving two Boeing 737 jets at 10am on 9 August.

"The incident occurred when a Virgin Australia 737 was cleared by air traffic control (ATC) for take-off from Sydney’s runway 34L," ATSB said in a statement to SBS News.

"As the crew applied thrust for take-off, they observed a Qantas 737 crossing the runway ahead of them on taxiway Lima.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Upon seeing the Qantas aircraft, the Virgin Australia crew reduced thrust and the aircraft came to a stop, roughly a kilometre from the intersection."

The Qantas jet crossed the takeoff path of the Virgin flight, forcing ATC to cancel the latter's departure clearance "at the same time".

The ATSB said investigations were already underway, with evidence being gathered and interviews with the involved parties expected to be conducted.

On Sunday, a Jetstar flight had to slam on the brakes to avoid hitting a Qatar Airways plane being towed across the tarmac.

The two weekend incidents come just weeks after two Qantas flights, with ATC permission, managed to narrowly avoid contact in Sydney at the end of July.

All three incidents are under investigation by the national transport safety watchdog, which operates "no fault" fact-finding missions in order to prevent similar incidents from occurring, rather than to take punitive action.

On Monday, ATSB chief commissioner Angus Mitchell said that the Jetstar-Qatar incident "could have been far more serious" and that incidents like that "shouldn't happen".

"We do have an aviation sector that is the envy of the world. That's not to say that with incidents like this, we don't take them seriously to improve," he said.

"But aircraft movements, whether it be in a busy airport or in the skies, are incredibly well coordinated here in Australia."

Airservices Australia — the government-owned corporation responsible for managing air traffic control across much of the country — admitted on Monday that it had been too reliant on overtime staffing hours.

body.en:
Imagine paying a mortgage from today until 2066. For some Australians, that could become a reality as more lenders offer 40-year home loans.

In the last few years, an increasing number of smaller lenders in Australia have begun to offer these extended loan terms — a decade longer than the standard 30-year term.

Australian bank AMP was the latest to jump on the bandwagon, recently announcing a new 40-year mortgage product for investors.

It joins a relatively small list of competitors including Credit Union SA, Unity Bank, Great Southern Bank, RACQ Bank, Bank of Us, Liberty and Pepper Money.

Sally Tindall, data insights director at financial comparison site Canstar, told SBS News many of the 40-year mortgages are geared towards younger people and first-home buyers.

Last year, a Finder survey found that 30 per cent of Australians would take out a 40-year mortgage if it reduced their monthly repayments to a more affordable level.

But experts warn there are major downsides that would-be borrowers should weigh.

With house prices at historic highs, a longer loan term can make it easier for some Australians to enter the housing market by reducing monthly repayments, improving their serviceability or increasing how much they can borrow.

According to an analysis by Canstar, an additional decade of repayments on a $600,000 mortgage could reduce a borrower's initial monthly repayments by around $288 but result in nearly $275,000 in extra interest over the life of the loan.

"It improves someone's chances of getting the green light on a loan that they might not have otherwise been able to afford," Tindall told SBS News.

"But really, if you are someone that is struggling to pay off a debt over 30 years, it's worth stopping and thinking, well, is the size of the amount I want to borrow too high for my financial situation?"

Last year, when Great Southern Bank introduced a new 40-year loan, its chief customer officer, Rolf Stromsoe, suggested the product could be a stepping stone for first-home buyers, allowing them to enter the market before ultimately refinancing.

"As their needs evolve and their earnings capacity changes, they may refinance any number of times — but this is the loan that can start it all," he said.

But Tindall warned that refinancing may be a challenge with this type of product, given the limited pool of lenders that offer them and their high-risk profile.

body.en:
Australians will have to wait until the middle of next year to see the first results of the 2026 Census, with the full dataset not expected until 2028.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) will release the results in three stages, starting in mid-2027 and continuing into the following year.

Jenny Telford, the ABS' general manager of the Census and population statistics, explained why it takes around 10 months to release the first batch of results.

"June 2027, it might sound like a long time away, but Australia is a really big country," she said on Thursday.

"It takes us quite a while to bring in every paper form from every part of remote Australia. Lots of work ahead of us, but June next year is when we'll release that picture of the nation."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Over eight million completed Census forms had been received by Wednesday morning, the ABS confirmed, accounting for over two-thirds of Australians.

The first release is scheduled for June 2027, less than a year after Census night. It will include most Census topics and cover almost all geographic areas.

This first release will provide a broad picture of Australia, including population characteristics such as age, sex recorded at birth, gender and sexual orientation.

It will also include information on family composition, relationships, country of birth, ancestry, language, religion, education, income, housing, health, disability, unpaid work and care, and other demographic characteristics.

This will add a range of employment and location-based information, including labour force status, occupation, industry, hours worked, place of work and methods of travelling to work.

This release will be particularly useful for understanding how Australia's communities function economically, including where people live and where they work. That information can help reveal commuting patterns and the links between residential areas and employment centres.

It will contain information requiring additional processing, including distance to work, estimates of homelessness and the Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA).

SEIFA provides a way to compare areas based on their relative socioeconomic characteristics and can be particularly useful for governments and organisations when identifying areas of greater need and informing decisions about funding and services.

The staged approach is designed to give the ABS time to process, check and protect the data before it is published.

title.en: One of Australia's most senior Catholic figures convicted of sexual abuse crimes

summary.en: Years after allegations first emerged, the Bishop of Broome has been found guilty.

body.en:
A former high-ranking Catholic known for hosting alcohol-fuelled parties has been convicted of sexually abusing two young Aboriginal men.

Former Bishop of Broome Christopher Alan Saunders, 76, was found guilty of 13 sex offences on Thursday   following a jury trial in the West Australian District Court.

The offending between 2008 and 2019 included one count of sexual penetration without consent and a dozen unlawful and indecent assault charges.

He was acquitted of six other charges, including two counts of indecently dealing with a child over 16 under his authority and four counts of unlawful and indecent assault.

Saunders was ordained as the second Broome bishop in 1996 and presided over 13 schools and nine parishes, before stepping aside in 2020 when the sex abuse claims became public.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Unless acquitted on appeal, Saunders would be the highest-ranking Catholic in Australia convicted of sexual abuse while a member of the clergy.

The late Cardinal George Pell was found guilty in 2018 but later acquitted by the High Court of raping one choirboy and molesting another in 1996.

Prosecutors said Saunders, known as Brother B by his victims, put on alcohol-fuelled parties at Catholic Church-owned properties to get access to Aboriginal boys and men so he could sexually assault them.

"The accused had a sexual interest in young Aboriginal men and a tendency to act on that interest when the opportunity presented itself," prosecutor Adam Ebell said.

Saunders, who studied law before becoming the first diocesan priest ordained in WA's Kimberley region in 1976, exploited the power imbalance between himself and the younger men, he said.

The main complainant, who cannot be named for legal reasons, said he was aged 16 when the then-bishop started grooming him at a Broome home in regular visits during which he was given alcohol.

The interactions over the decade that followed involved kissing, naked wrestling, touching of private areas and penetrative sex, he said.

His lawyer Tony Hager attacked the three complainants, saying they were convicted criminals with long records who had abused alcohol and drugs during their lives, which impacted their memories.

Saunders was initially on trial for 30 sexual assault charges, but four charges related to a child under the age of 13 were removed from the prosecution on the first day of proceedings.

He was acquitted of a further seven charges mid-trial due to insufficient evidence being presented to the jury.

title.en: 130,000 people: One Nation clarifies plan for major migration cut
title.zh: 13万人：一国党澄清大规模移民削减计划

summary.en: A key detail behind One Nation's headline migration pledge has now come into focus.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
One Nation has confirmed its plan to significantly limit migration to Australia to 130,000 people a year will be based on the net overseas migration forecast.

Australia's migration level has become one of the most combustible debates in federal politics, as the nation faces a housing shortage and pressure on services, particularly in suburban areas.

Migration experts have warned of the dangers of political parties attempting to blame migrants for a lack of homes , arguing that migrant workforces will be essential to building the required housing stock .

The net overseas migration measure is forecast by projecting how many people will enter and depart the country; it includes returning Australians.

This measure includes visitor and tourist options, family and partner visas, working holidaymakers, skilled migration, plus refugee and humanitarian programs.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Under Labor, net overseas migration reached a record high of 556,000 in 2023, following the COVID-19 pandemic.

But Labor has moved to tighten restrictions, projecting net overseas migration to fall to 225,000 people by the 2027-2028 financial year.

The government is preparing to unveil a plan to wind back migration settings to ensure the net overseas migration forecast is met.

Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke was set to unveil that plan at the National Press Club last week — but it was put on hold after cabinet jitters about the political implications of cuts to certain programs.

According to its website, One Nation's policy is "capping visas at 130,000 per year to ease pressure on housing, wages, and infrastructure".

A One Nation spokesperson has confirmed to SBS World News that the cap of 130,000 will be on net overseas migration.

That is a dramatic reduction from the current numbers, which the government maintains would affect a range of visa categories and impede productivity nationwide.

But One Nation leader Pauline Hanson maintains the government has been too reliant on migration to keep the economy going.

Meanwhile, Nationals and senior Liberals have distanced themselves from a figure the Opposition's housing minister suggested cutting immigration to.

Andrew Bragg used a National Press Club speech on Wednesday to argue for a Coalition policy of capping net overseas migration at 180,000.

But Nationals leader Matt Canavan has already cautioned against any moves that would reduce the workforce in regional areas.

On Thursday, Opposition leader Angus Taylor said Bragg was expressing personal views and didn't run the speech by him before he delivered it.

summary.en: Australia's next total solar eclipse will deliver a rare spectacle across parts of the country.

body.en:
As millions turned out to see the total solar eclipse over Europe, some Australians may be wondering when it will be our turn to enjoy such a spectacle.

If you're among them, there's some good news: Australia's next total solar eclipse is on the horizon, and it will bring a rare celestial spectacle to parts of the country.

A total solar eclipse is when the moon's orbit passes between the Earth and the sun. For a few moments, the three planetary bodies align. The moon almost perfectly blocks the sun from view, plunging the planet below into a brief darkness.

That's quite different to the partial solar eclipse. In a partial solar eclipse, the orbits of the Earth, moon, and sun align, but the moon only obscures part of the sun.

It's rare for total solar eclipses to happen anywhere. It's rarer still for them to happen in Australia. There have been just five total solar eclipses visible from Australia in the last 50 years — two close together in 1974 and 1976, then long gaps between eclipses in 2002, 2013 and 2023.

Even then, the word "visible" has done some heavy lifting. Most total eclipses only graze the Australian continent, passing over a northern or southern tip. The 2023 total eclipse, for instance, passed just off the North West Cape region of Western Australia and then transited northeast over Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

The 2028 total solar eclipse, also referred to as the Great Australasian Eclipse in some quarters, will start on Saturday 22 July 2028. As the name suggests, the moon will completely obscure the sun for those on the ground.

It will pass south-west across the Australian continent from the Kimberley in northern Western Australia. The eclipse path will then move across the Northern Territory, south-western Queensland and rural NSW, and finally arrive directly over Sydney.

For those in the Kimberley, the total eclipse will begin at around 11am AWST. In Sydney, the total eclipse will start at 2pm AEST. It will last for around four minutes as the moon passes in front of the sun.

To put the rarity of an eclipse path of this kind into context, 2028 will be the first time Sydney has experienced a total solar eclipse since 1857. According to NASA, it won't happen again for another 800 years — 3 June 2858.

When the 2028 eclipse passes over Dunedin in New Zealand later that afternoon, it will be the first to do so since 1163.

But what about Australian cities other than Sydney? Will you be able to see the eclipse?
